Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `Option`

```bastio
enum Option[T] { Some(T), None }
```

A value that may be missing. Functions in core return it for "not found",
"does not parse" and "no such key".

### `Span`

```bastio
struct Span { start: u64, end: u64 }
```

Bytes `start..end` of some byte string. core works on spans instead of
copies wherever it can: splitting and trimming return spans.

## Functions

### `opt_or`

```bastio
fn opt_or[T](o: Option[T], d: T) -> T
  ensures o is Option::Some ==> result == o.Some
  ensures o is Option::None ==> result == d
```

The payload of `o`, or `d` when there is none.

Example:

```bastio
let found = Option[u64]::Some(8080);
let missing = Option[u64]::None;
let a = opt_or[u64](found, 80);
let b = opt_or[u64](missing, 80);
assert a == 8080 && b == 80;   // both proved from the contract
```
